h: Tiny Monkeys and a Tidy Day on the Teign
p: Shaldon Wildlife Trust runs as a charity, and that conservation focus is what gives it its heart. A lot of the collection is made up of small South American primates like tamarins and marmosets, many of them part of breeding programmes for species that are struggling in the wild. They're fast, noisy and full of character, so it pays to stand still at each enclosure for a minute or two and let them come to you. Patience gets you the best views.

Because it's small, think of the zoo as one part of a wider Shaldon day rather than the whole thing. Parking at the Ness car park puts you in a good spot for the zoo, the beach and the headland all at once. Next door on the hillside you'll find Homeyards Botanical Gardens, a peaceful terraced garden with sea views that's a nice quiet spot for a sit-down.

Across the water, Teignmouth has a sandy town beach, a pier with old-school amusements and the Back Beach on the estuary, where boats are pulled up on the sand and you can watch the comings and goings of the harbour. The train line along the coast here, past Dawlish and Teignmouth, runs right along the sea wall and is one of the most scenic stretches of railway in the country, so it's worth a ride if you're arriving by rail.

Fancy a little more wildlife? Head along the coast road towards Torquay and you'll reach RSPB Labrador Bay, clifftop farmland where the rare cirl bunting has made a comeback. Pack a picnic and you've got a gentle, nature-filled Devon day.
